notes.front: In Microsoft Purview, what is data classification?
notes.back: Identifying and tagging the sensitive and important information across your data estate, so you know what you hold.
notes.explanation: Knowing your data is what lets you check it is handled in line with compliance requirements.
notes.example: Like sorting a filing room into “public”, “internal” and “payroll” boxes, but done automatically across mailboxes and sites.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the data classification capabilities of Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Describe the data classification capabilities of Microsoft Purview Information Protection”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is a sensitive information type (SIT)?
notes.back: A pattern-based classifier that detects a kind of sensitive information, such as credit card or bank account numbers.
notes.explanation: It finds sensitive items by matching patterns rather than by understanding what a document is about.
notes.example: Like a sniffer dog trained on one scent, but the scent is the format of a passport number.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the data classification capabilities of Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Sensitive information types”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is an exact data match (EDM) sensitive information type?
notes.back: A custom SIT that looks for the exact values held in a database of your sensitive information.
notes.explanation: It matches real values, so it suits highly specific data such as patient record numbers or product codes.
notes.example: Like a guest list at a door: only names actually on the list count, not anything that merely looks like a name.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the data classification capabilities of Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Sensitive information types”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is a trainable classifier in Microsoft Purview?
notes.back: A classifier that uses AI and machine learning to recognise content by what it is, not by matching patterns.
notes.explanation: It suits data unique to an organisation, such as its own kinds of contracts, where patterns alone are not enough.
notes.example: Like a new clerk who learns to spot a supplier invoice after seeing many examples, rather than checking for one number format.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the data classification capabilities of Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Trainable classifiers”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is content explorer in Microsoft Purview?
notes.back: A tool giving a current snapshot of items that carry a sensitivity label or retention label, or match a sensitive information type.
notes.explanation: Admins with the right roles can drill down to review the scanned content itself in places such as Exchange, SharePoint and OneDrive.
notes.example: Like a warehouse stock report showing what is on each shelf today, but for labelled and sensitive files.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the data classification capabilities of Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Content explorer”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is activity explorer in Microsoft Purview?
notes.back: A tool showing what labelled or discovered content exists and what users are doing with it.
notes.explanation: It tracks actions such as label changes and copying files to removable media or network shares.
notes.example: Like a building’s door-entry log, which records who went where, rather than a list of what is in each room.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the data classification capabilities of Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Activity explorer”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is a sensitivity label in Microsoft Purview?
notes.back: A label that classifies and can protect content, applied like a stamp that travels with the content wherever it goes.
notes.explanation: It is meant to protect data without getting in the way of productivity and collaboration.
notes.example: Like a “Confidential” stamp on a paper file, but one that can also lock the file so only named people can open it.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe sensitivity labels and policies in Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Sensitivity labels”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is a sensitivity label policy?
notes.back: The means of publishing sensitivity labels to chosen users or groups, so the labels appear in their Office apps.
notes.explanation: Creating a label does not make it available; it must be published before people and services can use it.
notes.example: Like adding a new form to a company intranet for one department only, so only its staff can pick it.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe sensitivity labels and policies in Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Sensitivity label policies”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is mandatory labelling in a sensitivity label policy?
notes.back: A setting that makes users apply a label before they can save a document, send an email, or create a site or group.
notes.explanation: It is one of the settings a sensitivity label policy can turn on.
notes.example: Like a web form that will not submit until you pick a category from the drop-down.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe sensitivity labels and policies in Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Sensitivity label policies”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is data loss prevention (DLP) in Microsoft Purview?
notes.back: Policies that identify, monitor and automatically protect sensitive items, so they are not shared inappropriately.
notes.explanation: You put DLP in place by defining and applying DLP policies across services, apps and devices.
notes.example: Like a shop’s security tag alarm that sounds at the door, but for sensitive data leaving by email, chat or copying.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe data loss prevention in Microsoft Purview, “Describe data loss prevention in Microsoft Purview”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is a policy tip in DLP?
notes.back: A pop-up notice warning users that they may be about to share a sensitive item inappropriately.
notes.explanation: It can also explain why a policy was triggered, and may let the user override a block with a justification.
notes.example: Like a sat-nav warning “you are entering a low-emission zone” before you turn, rather than just a fine afterwards.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe data loss prevention in Microsoft Purview, “Protective actions of DLP policies”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is endpoint data loss prevention?
notes.back: DLP for sensitive items stored on Windows 10, Windows 11 or macOS devices, auditing and managing what users do with them.
notes.explanation: It extends DLP from cloud services to activity on the devices themselves, such as printing or copying.
notes.example: Like the office security tag system, but fitted to each laptop instead of only at the building’s exit.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe data loss prevention in Microsoft Purview, “What is endpoint data loss prevention?”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is Microsoft Purview Data Lifecycle Management?
notes.back: Purview tools to keep the content you need and delete the content you do not.
notes.explanation: Keeping and deleting emails, documents and messages is often needed for compliance and regulatory requirements.
notes.example: Like a household rule to keep tax papers for a set time and shred them after, but applied automatically to mail and files.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Data Lifecycle Management, “Describe Data Lifecycle Management”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is a retention policy in Microsoft Purview?
notes.back: A way to give the same retention settings to content at site or mailbox level.
notes.explanation: Items inherit the settings from the container the policy names.
notes.example: Like a rule that every folder in one filing cabinet is kept for three years, whatever is in it.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Data Lifecycle Management, “Retention policies and retention labels”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is a retention label in Microsoft Purview?
notes.back: A way to give retention settings to a single item, such as a folder, document or email.
notes.explanation: It works at item level, unlike a retention policy, which works on a whole container.
notes.example: Like a “keep until 2035” sticker on one file, rather than a rule for the whole cabinet.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Data Lifecycle Management, “Retention policies and retention labels”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is a retention label policy?
notes.back: The policy that publishes retention labels, naming which locations and users can apply them.
notes.explanation: It lets organisations roll labels out in a controlled way to the right people.
notes.example: Like handing a stamp set only to the records clerks in two offices, not to everyone.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Data Lifecycle Management, “Retention label policies”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is mailbox archiving in Data Lifecycle Management?
notes.back: Extra mailbox storage for users, with auto-expanding archiving for mailboxes that outgrow the standard limit.
notes.explanation: It helps prevent losing email because of storage limits.
notes.example: Like a self-storage unit that grows as you fill it, attached to your home mailbox.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Data Lifecycle Management, “Additional data lifecycle management capabilities”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is an inactive mailbox?
notes.back: The mailbox of someone who has left, kept after their account is deleted because it was put on hold first.
notes.explanation: It is retained indefinitely, which supports legal and regulatory requirements.
notes.example: Like keeping a former employee’s paper files in the archive room after their desk is cleared.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Data Lifecycle Management, “Additional data lifecycle management capabilities”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is Microsoft Purview Records Management?
notes.back: A solution for managing regulatory, legal and business-critical records, building on Data Lifecycle Management.
notes.explanation: It adds more control for high-value items: items declared as records have restricted actions and are tracked through their lifecycle.
notes.example: Like a solicitor’s strongroom for signed deeds, compared with the general filing room.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Purview Records Management, “Describe Microsoft Purview Records Management”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is event-based retention?
notes.back: Retention whose period starts when a specified event happens, not from a fixed date such as creation.
notes.explanation: It suits items whose lifecycle is tied to business events.
notes.example: Like a warranty clock that starts when you take delivery, not when the item was made.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Purview Records Management, “Event-based retention”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is a disposition review?
notes.back: A check before permanent deletion, where chosen reviewers approve the deletion or extend the retention period.
notes.explanation: It gives assurance that no important records are deleted by accident.
notes.example: Like a second signature needed before old archive boxes go to the shredder.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Purview Records Management, “Disposition reviews”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is a file plan in Records Management?
notes.back: A tool for managing retention requirements in a structured way, with all retention labels in one place.
notes.explanation: It suits organisations that already have retention schedules to align with Purview.
notes.example: Like a master index of every records rule in the company, with who set it and why.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Purview Records Management, “File plan”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is data governance, as Microsoft Purview describes it?
notes.back: Managing data so it is secure and compliant, and also visible and useful to the people who need it.
notes.explanation: Historically it was a defence mechanism; good governance also reconnects the business with its data.
notes.example: Like running a library: guarding rare books, but also cataloguing them so readers can find them.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the concepts and benefits of data governance, “Describe the concepts and benefits of data governance”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is Microsoft Purview Unified Catalog?
notes.back: A platform for data governance that builds on metadata captured by Data Map.
notes.explanation: Its features, such as governance domains and data products, align with data governance principles.
notes.example: Like an online shop’s catalogue for a company’s data, with owners, descriptions and rules for each item.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Purview Unified Catalog, “Describe Microsoft Purview Unified Catalog”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Unified Catalog, what is a governance domain?
notes.back: A boundary, such as Marketing or Finance, that organises the data estate by business concept for shared governance, ownership and discovery.
notes.explanation: It gives context to data assets, data products, glossary terms and other business concepts.
notes.example: Like a department in a department store, grouping related goods under one manager.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Purview Unified Catalog, “Governance domains”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Unified Catalog, what is a data product?
notes.back: A business construct with a name, description, owners and a list of associated data assets.
notes.explanation: It gives context for its assets and a use case for data consumers.
notes.example: Like a meal kit that bundles all the ingredients and the recipe card, rather than loose items on shelves.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Purview Unified Catalog, “Data products”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Unified Catalog, what is a glossary term?
notes.back: A concept defining the organisation’s business, processes or systems, applied to data to give business context.
notes.explanation: Terms also carry policies on how the data should be managed, governed and made discoverable.
notes.example: Like a company style guide entry that says what “active customer” means here, and how that data may be used.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Purview Unified Catalog, “Glossary terms”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Unified Catalog, what is a critical data element (CDE)?
notes.back: A logical grouping of an important piece of information found across the data estate.
notes.explanation: Quality rules and access policies can be attached to it to help secure sensitive information.
notes.example: Like one “date of birth” definition that covers the BirthDate and born_on fields in different systems.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Purview Unified Catalog, “Critical data elements”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Microsoft Purview, what are objectives and key results (OKRs)?
notes.back: Trackable business objectives tied to governance domains and data products.
notes.explanation: They link data products to real business aims, underlining the value of business data.
notes.example: Like a sales team’s quarterly target, but pinned to the data products that feed it.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Purview Unified Catalog, “OKRs”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Unified Catalog, what is health management?
notes.back: Features, including health controls and health actions, for monitoring and improving data governance health.
notes.explanation: Health controls track progress; health actions list steps to raise the health score.
notes.example: Like a car dashboard with warning lights plus a service checklist.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Purview Unified Catalog, “Health management”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Microsoft Purview, what is Data Quality?
notes.back: A capability that lets governance domain and data owners assess and oversee the quality of their data.
notes.explanation: It supports targeted actions to improve that quality.
notes.example: Like a factory inspection line that checks each batch, but for the accuracy of data sets.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Purview Unified Catalog, “Data quality”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Where do admins find Microsoft Purview’s data classification and explorer capabilities?
notes.back: In the Microsoft Purview portal.
notes.explanation: The explorers sit in the Explorers section under Information Protection.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the data classification capabilities of Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Describe the data classification capabilities of Microsoft Purview Information Protection”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which part of a sensitive information type is the main thing it looks for, such as a regular expression or a keyword list?
notes.back: The primary element.
notes.explanation: It can also be a keyword dictionary or a function, and a regular expression may carry a checksum validation.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the data classification capabilities of Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Sensitive information types”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which part of a sensitive information type provides corroborating evidence that raises confidence in a match?
notes.back: Supporting elements.
notes.explanation: A telling keyword found near a candidate number makes it likelier to be the real thing.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the data classification capabilities of Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Sensitive information types”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which part of a sensitive information type reflects how much supporting evidence was found, at low, medium or high?
notes.back: The confidence level.
notes.explanation: It sets how aggressively the SIT flags possible matches.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the data classification capabilities of Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Sensitive information types”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which part of a sensitive information type sets how close supporting evidence must be to the primary element?
notes.back: Proximity, measured in characters.
notes.explanation: Evidence too far away does not count towards the match.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the data classification capabilities of Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Sensitive information types”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is the trade-off of a high confidence level in a sensitive information type?
notes.back: Fewer false positives, but it might miss more true matches.
notes.explanation: The confidence level sets how aggressively a SIT flags potential matches.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the data classification capabilities of Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Sensitive information types”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which kind of sensitive information type does Microsoft create and maintain, and shows in the Purview portal by default?
notes.back: Built-in sensitive information types.
notes.explanation: You cannot edit them directly, but you can copy one as a template for your own variation.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the data classification capabilities of Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Sensitive information types”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which kind of sensitive information type detects person names, physical addresses and medical terms and conditions?
notes.back: Named entity sensitive information types.
notes.explanation: They come in unbundled forms with a narrow focus and bundled forms that detect a whole class.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the data classification capabilities of Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Sensitive information types”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: How does a bundled named entity SIT differ from an unbundled one?
notes.back: Bundled detects all matches in a class, such as addresses worldwide; unbundled is narrow, such as one country’s addresses.
notes.explanation: Both are forms of named entity sensitive information type.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the data classification capabilities of Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Sensitive information types”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which kind of sensitive information type do you build yourself from regular expressions, keywords and keyword dictionaries?
notes.back: Custom sensitive information types.
notes.explanation: You create them when the built-in types do not meet your needs, such as for your own staff numbers.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the data classification capabilities of Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Sensitive information types”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which kind of sensitive information type references exact values from a database of your sensitive information?
notes.back: Exact data match (EDM) sensitive information types.
notes.explanation: They are the fourth of the four kinds Purview supports.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the data classification capabilities of Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Sensitive information types”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In which Microsoft Purview solutions are sensitive information types used? Give two.
notes.back: Any two of: DLP policies, sensitivity labels, retention labels, insider risk management, communication compliance, auto-labelling policies.
notes.explanation: The same SIT definitions are reused across these solutions.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the data classification capabilities of Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Sensitive information types”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Can sensitive information types detect sensitive data that a user types into Microsoft 365 Copilot?
notes.back: Yes. SITs and trainable classifiers can identify it in prompts and responses of AI apps.
notes.explanation: The same SITs that protect items in email and documents apply to the AI interaction.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the data classification capabilities of Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Data classification and AI interactions”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which type of trainable classifier can you use straight away without any extra training?
notes.back: Pre-trained classifiers, created by Microsoft and shown as Ready to use.
notes.explanation: They cover categories such as financial documents, legal content, résumés and harassment.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the data classification capabilities of Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Trainable classifiers”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is the first step in creating a custom trainable classifier?
notes.back: Seeding: giving samples that definitely are in the category and samples that definitely are not.
notes.explanation: Purview builds the classifier’s prediction model from those samples.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the data classification capabilities of Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Trainable classifiers”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: After seeding a custom trainable classifier, when can you publish it?
notes.back: Once you have verified its results and its accuracy score has stabilised.
notes.explanation: Verification means sorting its results into true and false positives and negatives to improve the model.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the data classification capabilities of Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Trainable classifiers”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which items can trainable classifiers not work with?
notes.back: Encrypted items.
notes.explanation: Microsoft notes that classifiers only work with items that are not encrypted.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the data classification capabilities of Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Trainable classifiers”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Where can trainable classifiers be used as conditions? Give two.
notes.back: Any two of: sensitivity label auto-labelling, retention label policies, communication compliance policies, DLP policies.
notes.explanation: A classifier can decide when those policies act on an item.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the data classification capabilities of Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Trainable classifiers”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What does content explorer help admins understand? Give two.
notes.back: Any two of: how many items are classified and which types apply; where sensitive data is stored; how it is spread across the organisation.
notes.explanation: These are views of what is held now, by location and label.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the data classification capabilities of Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Content explorer”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Why is access to content explorer highly restricted?
notes.back: It lets the viewer read the contents of scanned files.
notes.explanation: A user needs one of the designated content explorer role groups to use it.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the data classification capabilities of Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Content explorer”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which explorer would show that a user changed a document’s label from Confidential to Public?
notes.back: Activity explorer.
notes.explanation: It monitors document-level activities such as label changes and downgrades.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the data classification capabilities of Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Activity explorer”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: From which source does activity explorer receive signals about printing or copying on Windows and macOS devices?
notes.back: Endpoint data loss prevention.
notes.explanation: That gives activity explorer visibility of activity on the devices themselves.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the data classification capabilities of Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Activity explorer”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What do admins use activity explorer to judge?
notes.back: Whether the controls already in place work, and where more protection policy may be needed.
notes.explanation: Its filters show all the details for a label, including file types, users and activities.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the data classification capabilities of Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Activity explorer”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which property of sensitivity labels lets admins create categories such as Personal, Public and Highly Confidential?
notes.back: They are customisable.
notes.explanation: Each organisation defines the categories that fit it.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe sensitivity labels and policies in Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Sensitivity labels”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which property of sensitivity labels lets third-party apps read them and apply their own protection?
notes.back: They are stored in clear text in the content’s metadata.
notes.explanation: Because the label is readable, other services can act on it.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe sensitivity labels and policies in Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Sensitivity labels”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which property of sensitivity labels means the label and its protection settings move with an email or document?
notes.back: They are persistent.
notes.explanation: The label stored in the item’s metadata becomes the basis for applying and enforcing policies.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe sensitivity labels and policies in Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Sensitivity labels”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: How many sensitivity labels can an item carry at one time?
notes.back: One.
notes.explanation: Each item that supports sensitivity labels can have only a single label applied at any given time.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe sensitivity labels and policies in Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Sensitivity labels”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: When a sensitivity label encrypts content, what can you specify?
notes.back: Which users or groups may do which actions, and for how long.
notes.explanation: Encryption keeps unauthorised people out of emails, meeting invites and documents.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe sensitivity labels and policies in Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “What sensitivity labels can do”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which content markings can a sensitivity label add in Office apps?
notes.back: Watermarks, headers or footers.
notes.explanation: Headers and footers work on emails, meeting invites and documents.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe sensitivity labels and policies in Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “What sensitivity labels can do”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Can a sensitivity label add a watermark to an email?
notes.back: No. Watermarks go on documents and Loop components and pages, not on email or meeting invites.
notes.explanation: Headers and footers are the markings available for emails.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe sensitivity labels and policies in Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “What sensitivity labels can do”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: How can a sensitivity label be applied without the user choosing it first?
notes.back: Automatically in Office apps, or by recommending it to the user, when chosen sensitive information types are found.
notes.explanation: Admins pick which types of sensitive information trigger the label.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe sensitivity labels and policies in Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “What sensitivity labels can do”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: When a sensitivity label protects a container such as a Teams team or SharePoint site, does it label the documents inside?
notes.back: No. It protects content by controlling access to the container, not by labelling each document.
notes.explanation: The container settings govern who can get in, rather than stamping the items.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe sensitivity labels and policies in Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “What sensitivity labels can do”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which sensitivity label setting helps prevent oversharing from SharePoint and OneDrive?
notes.back: Setting the default sharing link type for sites and documents.
notes.explanation: It controls the default scope and permissions when users share documents.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe sensitivity labels and policies in Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “What sensitivity labels can do”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Must a sensitivity label apply protection settings?
notes.back: No. It can simply classify content as a tag that persists and roams with it.
notes.explanation: Such a classification still produces usage reports and activity data for sensitive content.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe sensitivity labels and policies in Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “What sensitivity labels can do”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which sensitivity label scope is selected by default for every new label?
notes.back: Files & other data assets.
notes.explanation: It covers Word, Excel and PowerPoint files and Microsoft Fabric items; Emails, Meetings and Groups & sites are the other scopes.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe sensitivity labels and policies in Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Label scopes”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which sensitivity label scope covers calendar events and Teams meeting options, and needs two other scopes selected too?
notes.back: Meetings; it also needs the Files and Emails scopes.
notes.explanation: Microsoft notes many labelling features need Files and Emails together, since emails often carry attachments.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe sensitivity labels and policies in Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Label scopes”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which sensitivity label scope protects SharePoint sites, Microsoft 365 groups and Loop workspaces?
notes.back: Groups & sites.
notes.explanation: Labels at this scope control the container’s access settings but do not label the items inside.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe sensitivity labels and policies in Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Label scopes”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: When Microsoft 365 Copilot writes a response from several labelled items, which label does the response inherit?
notes.back: The most restrictive one, typically the highest-priority label.
notes.explanation: Copilot recognises and honours sensitivity labels on the data it draws on.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe sensitivity labels and policies in Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Sensitivity labels and Microsoft 365 Copilot”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Before Copilot uses content encrypted by a sensitivity label, what does it check?
notes.back: That the user has the permissions needed to access and reference that content.
notes.explanation: That way the label’s protection still holds in AI-assisted work.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe sensitivity labels and policies in Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Sensitivity labels and Microsoft 365 Copilot”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: To whom can a sensitivity label policy publish labels? Give two.
notes.back: Any two of: specific users, distribution groups, Microsoft 365 groups in Microsoft Entra ID, among others.
notes.explanation: The policy decides who can see the labels in their apps.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe sensitivity labels and policies in Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Sensitivity label policies”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A label policy applies a default label to new documents. Can users change it?
notes.back: Yes. Users can always change the default label if they think the item is mislabelled.
notes.explanation: The default applies to all new emails and documents the chosen users create.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe sensitivity labels and policies in Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Sensitivity label policies”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which label policy setting makes a user explain why before removing a label or switching to a less sensitive one?
notes.back: Requiring justification for label changes.
notes.explanation: The user is prompted for a reason before the change completes.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe sensitivity labels and policies in Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Sensitivity label policies”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which label policy setting helps users understand what each label means and how to use it?
notes.back: Linking users to a custom help page.
notes.explanation: It is one of the five things a sensitivity label policy lets admins do.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe sensitivity labels and policies in Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Sensitivity label policies”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which device operating systems can DLP policies protect as endpoints?
notes.back: Windows 10, Windows 11 and macOS (the three latest released versions).
notes.explanation: These are the endpoint locations listed for DLP.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe data loss prevention in Microsoft Purview, “Describe data loss prevention in Microsoft Purview”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Can DLP protect sensitive items stored on premises?
notes.back: Yes: on-premises file shares and on-premises SharePoint.
notes.explanation: DLP locations are not limited to cloud services.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe data loss prevention in Microsoft Purview, “Describe data loss prevention in Microsoft Purview”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Besides Microsoft 365 services and Office apps, where else can DLP policies apply? Give two.
notes.back: Any two of: endpoints, non-Microsoft cloud apps, on-premises file shares and SharePoint, Microsoft Fabric workspaces, Microsoft Edge for Business.
notes.explanation: Edge for Business covers inline web traffic to unmanaged cloud apps.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe data loss prevention in Microsoft Purview, “Describe data loss prevention in Microsoft Purview”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: How does DLP detect sensitive items?
notes.back: By deep content analysis, not a simple text scan.
notes.explanation: It checks keywords, regular expressions, internal function validation, nearby secondary matches, and uses machine learning among other methods.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe data loss prevention in Microsoft Purview, “Describe data loss prevention in Microsoft Purview”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which DLP action blocks sharing but lets the user go ahead after giving a justification?
notes.back: Block with override, offered through a policy tip.
notes.explanation: The user’s justification is captured when they override.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe data loss prevention in Microsoft Purview, “Protective actions of DLP policies”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which DLP action stops the sharing with no way for the user to proceed?
notes.back: Blocking without the override option.
notes.explanation: It is the strictest of the sharing actions.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe data loss prevention in Microsoft Purview, “Protective actions of DLP policies”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: For sensitive data at rest, what protective action can DLP take?
notes.back: Lock the items and move them to a secure quarantine location.
notes.explanation: This action is specific to data at rest.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe data loss prevention in Microsoft Purview, “Protective actions of DLP policies”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What does DLP do with sensitive information in a Teams chat?
notes.back: It does not display it.
notes.explanation: This is the Teams-specific protective action.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe data loss prevention in Microsoft Purview, “Protective actions of DLP policies”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Where are all DLP-monitored activities recorded by default?
notes.back: In the Microsoft 365 Audit log, from which they are routed to activity explorer.
notes.explanation: Recording happens by default, without extra configuration.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe data loss prevention in Microsoft Purview, “Protective actions of DLP policies”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Besides the DLP alert management dashboard, where are DLP alerts sent?
notes.back: To the Microsoft Defender portal, where they are combined into incidents.
notes.explanation: Incidents give a fuller view of potential policy violations.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe data loss prevention in Microsoft Purview, “Protective actions of DLP policies”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What two ways can you start a DLP policy?
notes.back: From a predefined template, or as a custom policy.
notes.explanation: Either way, every DLP policy needs the same information.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe data loss prevention in Microsoft Purview, “DLP Policy information”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: When choosing the data a DLP policy monitors, what can a custom policy use? Give two.
notes.back: Any two of: sensitive information types, retention labels, sensitivity labels.
notes.explanation: Templates instead offer categories such as financial, medical and health, or privacy data.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe data loss prevention in Microsoft Purview, “DLP Policy information”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In a DLP policy, what does administrative scoping decide?
notes.back: Whether the policy covers all users and groups, or only the members of chosen administrative units.
notes.explanation: Administrative units let you give admins control over only part of the organisation.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe data loss prevention in Microsoft Purview, “DLP Policy information”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: After choosing the data, scope and locations for a DLP policy, what two things remain to choose?
notes.back: The conditions an item must match, and the protective action to take when they are met.
notes.explanation: These complete the five pieces of information every DLP policy needs.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe data loss prevention in Microsoft Purview, “DLP Policy information”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which user activities can endpoint DLP audit and manage? Give two.
notes.back: Any two of: creating, renaming, copying to removable media or network shares, printing, using unallowed apps and browsers.
notes.explanation: These are examples; the list in the source is not complete.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe data loss prevention in Microsoft Purview, “What is endpoint data loss prevention?”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: How can endpoint DLP help when users paste data into third-party generative AI sites in a browser?
notes.back: It can warn or block users from sharing sensitive information there, on onboarded Windows devices.
notes.explanation: A warning can let the user override with a justification.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe data loss prevention in Microsoft Purview, “Data loss prevention and AI interactions”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Teams content does DLP cover?
notes.back: Chat and channel messages, in the message or a file, including private channels.
notes.explanation: As with Exchange and SharePoint, policy tips show users why a policy triggered.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe data loss prevention in Microsoft Purview, “Data loss prevention in Microsoft Teams”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A hospital wants Purview to flag only the patient numbers that really exist in its records system, not anything formatted like one. Which kind of sensitive information type fits?
notes.back: A: an exact data match (EDM) SIT.
notes.choices:
A) An exact data match (EDM) SIT
B) A named entity SIT
C) A custom SIT built from a regular expression
D) A built-in SIT
notes.choicesExplained: D and C match by pattern, so look-alike numbers would also match. B detects names, addresses and medical terms, not record numbers.
notes.explanation: EDM references exact values from a database of sensitive information.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the data classification capabilities of Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Sensitive information types”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A SIT for staff numbers flags too many random eight-digit strings. You require the word “employee” within 50 characters. Which two SIT parts have you used?
notes.back: C: supporting elements and proximity.
notes.choices:
A) Confidence level and bundling
B) Primary element and checksum
C) Supporting elements and proximity
D) Keyword dictionary and function
notes.choicesExplained: B: the primary element is the number pattern itself. A: bundling applies to named entity SITs. D are possible forms of a primary element, not evidence near it.
notes.explanation: Supporting elements corroborate a match, and proximity sets how near they must be.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the data classification capabilities of Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Sensitive information types”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A law firm wants to find its own style of engagement letters, which have no fixed number or keyword pattern. What should it use?
notes.back: A: a custom trainable classifier seeded with sample letters.
notes.choices:
A) A custom trainable classifier seeded with sample letters
B) A keyword dictionary
C) A built-in sensitive information type
D) Content explorer
notes.choicesExplained: C and B depend on patterns or words, which these letters lack. D reports on items already classified; it does not classify.
notes.explanation: Trainable classifiers learn content by what it is and suit data unique to an organisation.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the data classification capabilities of Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Trainable classifiers”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: An admin must report how many files containing credit card numbers sit in each SharePoint site today. Which tool should she open?
notes.back: B: content explorer.
notes.choices:
A) Activity explorer
B) Content explorer
C) A sensitivity label policy
D) The Microsoft Purview Audit log
notes.choicesExplained: A shows what users did with content, not a count by location. C publishes labels. D records activities, not a snapshot of stored items.
notes.explanation: Content explorer gives a current snapshot of classified items by location and type.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the data classification capabilities of Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Content explorer”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A manager suspects staff are copying labelled files to removable drives before leaving. Which tool shows this activity?
notes.back: B: activity explorer.
notes.choices:
A) Content explorer
B) Activity explorer
C) A sensitivity label policy
D) A retention label
notes.choicesExplained: A shows what is stored and where, not what users did. C publishes labels to users. D keeps or deletes content.
notes.explanation: Activity explorer shows actions such as copying files to removable media.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the data classification capabilities of Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Activity explorer”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A partner’s document system reads the label on a file you sent and applies its own protection. Which sensitivity label property makes this possible?
notes.back: D: clear text in the metadata.
notes.choices:
A) Customisable
B) Container protection
C) Mandatory labelling
D) Clear text in the metadata
notes.choicesExplained: A lets you define your own categories. B controls access to sites and teams. C forces users to label; it does not make labels readable elsewhere.
notes.explanation: Labels stored in clear text can be read by third-party apps and services.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe sensitivity labels and policies in Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Sensitivity labels”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Legal wants every board paper to show “Board only” in the footer and be openable only by directors. What should it use?
notes.back: B: a sensitivity label with content marking and encryption.
notes.choices:
A) A retention label
B) A sensitivity label with content marking and encryption
C) A DLP policy tip
D) Content explorer
notes.choicesExplained: A keeps or deletes content; it does not protect it. C warns users when sharing. D reports on labelled items but does not protect them.
notes.explanation: Sensitivity labels can add headers or footers and encrypt content for named users.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe sensitivity labels and policies in Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “What sensitivity labels can do”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: New labels exist but finance staff cannot see them in Word. What is missing?
notes.back: C: a sensitivity label policy publishing them to finance.
notes.choices:
A) A DLP policy for finance
B) A trainable classifier
C) A sensitivity label policy publishing them to finance
D) A retention label policy
notes.choicesExplained: A protects against sharing but does not publish labels. B classifies content. D publishes retention labels, not sensitivity labels.
notes.explanation: Labels appear in Office apps only once a label policy publishes them to users or groups.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe sensitivity labels and policies in Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Sensitivity label policies”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Staff keep quietly removing the Confidential label from reports. Which label policy setting addresses this without blocking them outright?
notes.back: A: require a justification for label changes.
notes.choices:
A) Require a justification for label changes
B) Link to a custom help page
C) Publish the label to more groups
D) Apply a default label
notes.choicesExplained: B explains labels but does not check changes. C widens who sees the label. D only sets the starting label.
notes.explanation: Justification prompts users to explain removing or downgrading a label.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe sensitivity labels and policies in Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Sensitivity label policies”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A bank wants staff warned, but allowed to proceed with a reason, when they email a spreadsheet of account numbers outside the company. Which DLP action fits?
notes.back: D: block with override via a policy tip, capturing the justification.
notes.choices:
A) Hide the content in chat
B) Block without override
C) Move the file to quarantine
D) Block with override via a policy tip
notes.choicesExplained: A applies to Teams chat, not email. B leaves no way to proceed. C applies to data at rest, not email being sent.
notes.explanation: The override option lets the user continue after justifying the action.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe data loss prevention in Microsoft Purview, “Protective actions of DLP policies”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A company wants DLP to stop sensitive files being printed from staff laptops. Which kind of DLP location is this?
notes.back: C: endpoint devices, through endpoint DLP.
notes.choices:
A) Microsoft 365 services
B) On-premises file shares
C) Endpoint devices, through endpoint DLP
D) Non-Microsoft cloud apps
notes.choicesExplained: A covers services such as Exchange and SharePoint. B covers stored files on servers. D covers other cloud services.
notes.explanation: Endpoint DLP manages activities such as printing on Windows and macOS devices.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe data loss prevention in Microsoft Purview, “What is endpoint data loss prevention?”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: An admin building a DLP policy has chosen the data to monitor and the administrative scope. What does she choose next?
notes.back: B: the locations where the policy applies.
notes.choices:
A) The protective action
B) The locations where the policy applies
C) The sensitivity label scope
D) The conditions to match
notes.choicesExplained: A and D come after the locations in Microsoft’s order. C belongs to sensitivity labels, not DLP policies.
notes.explanation: Microsoft lists the information every DLP policy needs in this order: data, administrative scope, locations, conditions, then protective action.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe data loss prevention in Microsoft Purview, “DLP Policy information”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: How does content explorer differ from activity explorer?
notes.back: Content explorer shows what sensitive or labelled items exist and where; activity explorer shows what users do with them.
notes.explanation: One is a snapshot of stored items; the other tracks actions such as label changes.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the data classification capabilities of Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Understand and explore the data”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: How does a sensitive information type differ from a trainable classifier?
notes.back: A SIT matches patterns; a trainable classifier learns to recognise content by what it is.
notes.explanation: Trainable classifiers suit content where pattern matching alone is not enough.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the data classification capabilities of Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Trainable classifiers”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: How does a pre-trained classifier differ from a custom trainable classifier?
notes.back: Pre-trained is ready to use from Microsoft; custom must be seeded with your samples, verified and published.
notes.explanation: You build a custom one when the pre-trained options do not meet your needs.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the data classification capabilities of Microsoft Purview Information Protection, “Trainable classifiers”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Besides compliance, what does deleting content that no longer has business value do?
notes.back: It reduces your attack surface.
notes.explanation: Microsoft gives this alongside the compliance and regulatory reasons for deleting.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Data Lifecycle Management, “Describe Data Lifecycle Management”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: How do retention labels and policies help with rules that require content to be kept for a minimum time?
notes.back: They let you comply proactively with those industry regulations and internal policies.
notes.explanation: This is the first of three reasons Microsoft gives for using retention.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Data Lifecycle Management, “Retention policies and retention labels”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: How can retention reduce risk in litigation or after a security breach?
notes.back: By permanently deleting old content the organisation is no longer required to keep.
notes.explanation: This is the second of the three reasons Microsoft gives for using retention.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Data Lifecycle Management, “Retention policies and retention labels”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which reason for using retention concerns what users work with day to day?
notes.back: Making sure users work only with current, relevant content.
notes.explanation: Content that is no longer relevant should be deleted.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Data Lifecycle Management, “Retention policies and retention labels”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What does retaining content do in Microsoft Purview?
notes.back: Prevents its permanent deletion and keeps it available for eDiscovery.
notes.explanation: The other retention action, deleting, removes content permanently.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Data Lifecycle Management, “Retention policies and retention labels”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which retention outcome keeps content forever or for a set period, with no deletion step?
notes.back: Retain-only.
notes.explanation: It uses only the retaining action.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Data Lifecycle Management, “Retention policies and retention labels”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which retention outcome permanently deletes content after a set period, without first guaranteeing to keep it?
notes.back: Delete-only.
notes.explanation: It uses only the deleting action.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Data Lifecycle Management, “Retention policies and retention labels”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which retention outcome keeps content for a set period and then deletes it permanently?
notes.back: Retain and then delete.
notes.explanation: It combines both retention actions in sequence.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Data Lifecycle Management, “Retention policies and retention labels”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: When content has retention settings and a user edits or deletes it, what happens?
notes.back: A copy is kept automatically in a secure location; the content itself stays in its original place.
notes.explanation: People carry on as normal and usually need not know retention applies.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Data Lifecycle Management, “Retention policies and retention labels”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which workloads do retention settings work with? Give two.
notes.back: Any two of: SharePoint, OneDrive, Microsoft Teams, Viva Engage, Exchange.
notes.explanation: These are the five workloads Microsoft lists.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Data Lifecycle Management, “Retention policies and retention labels”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Can one retention policy cover several locations?
notes.back: Yes. A single policy can apply to multiple locations, or to specific locations or users.
notes.explanation: Items inherit the retention settings from the container the policy names.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Data Lifecycle Management, “Retention policies and retention labels”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: An item under a retention policy set to keep content is moved out of its container. What happens?
notes.back: A copy is kept in the workload’s secure location, but the settings do not travel with the item.
notes.explanation: Retention policy settings belong to the container, not the item.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Data Lifecycle Management, “Retention policies and retention labels”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: How many retention labels can an email or document have at once?
notes.back: One.
notes.explanation: An item can have only a single retention label at a time.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Data Lifecycle Management, “Retention policies and retention labels”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A document with a retention label moves to another site in the same Microsoft 365 tenant. Do its retention settings go with it?
notes.back: Yes, within the tenant; they do not persist if it leaves the tenant.
notes.explanation: Label settings travel with the content, unlike policy settings.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Data Lifecycle Management, “Retention policies and retention labels”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: How can a retention label get onto content? Give two.
notes.back: Any two of: users apply it manually, it is applied automatically when conditions match, a default label for SharePoint documents.
notes.explanation: Admins decide whether users may apply labels themselves.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Data Lifecycle Management, “Retention policies and retention labels”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which retention tool supports disposition review before content is permanently deleted?
notes.back: Retention labels.
notes.explanation: Microsoft lists disposition review support among the key points for retention labels.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Data Lifecycle Management, “Retention policies and retention labels”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Must you choose between retention policies and retention labels?
notes.back: No. You can use either one, or combine them.
notes.explanation: Policies set retention for whole sites or mailboxes and labels for single items, so the two can work together; labels are published through retention label policies.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Data Lifecycle Management, “Retention policies and retention labels”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What does a retention label policy help compliance managers achieve?
notes.back: Consistent application of retention settings across the organisation, with less manual tracking.
notes.explanation: It controls which locations and users can use the labels.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Data Lifecycle Management, “Retention label policies”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Where are prompts and responses from AI apps such as Microsoft 365 Copilot stored, so retention policies can act on them?
notes.back: In the user’s Exchange mailbox.
notes.explanation: That lets the same retention controls apply to AI content as to other data.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Data Lifecycle Management, “Additional data lifecycle management capabilities”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: How does Data Lifecycle Management work with Insider Risk Management?
notes.back: Retention labels can be applied automatically based on dynamic insider risk signals.
notes.explanation: This protects high-risk content from accidental or malicious deletion without manual work.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Data Lifecycle Management, “Additional data lifecycle management capabilities”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which features does Records Management include? Give two.
notes.back: Any two of: labelling content as a record, event-based retention, disposition review, proof of records deletion, exporting disposed-item information, among others.
notes.explanation: Retention and deletion policies can also be set within the record label.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Purview Records Management, “Describe Microsoft Purview Records Management”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: When content is labelled as a record, what happens? Give two.
notes.back: Any two of: certain activities are blocked, activities are logged, proof of disposition is kept at the end of retention.
notes.explanation: A retention label is what marks content as a record.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Purview Records Management, “Describe Microsoft Purview Records Management”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What must an administrator set up before items can be marked as records?
notes.back: Retention labels.
notes.explanation: Documents and emails are then marked as records based on those labels.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Purview Records Management, “Describe Microsoft Purview Records Management”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Once an item is marked as a regulatory record, can its label be removed?
notes.back: No. Nobody can remove it, not even a Global Administrator.
notes.explanation: Microsoft calls this the most important difference from an ordinary record.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Purview Records Management, “Describe Microsoft Purview Records Management”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: After a regulatory record label is applied, can its retention period be shortened?
notes.back: No.
notes.explanation: This is one of the extra restrictions regulatory records add.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Purview Records Management, “Describe Microsoft Purview Records Management”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Why is the regulatory record option not available by default?
notes.back: Its consequences can be irreversible, so an administrator must enable it with PowerShell.
notes.explanation: Microsoft advises using it only when necessary.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Purview Records Management, “Describe Microsoft Purview Records Management”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Standard retention counts from a fixed point, such as when an item was {{c1::created or last modified}}.
notes.back: created or last modified
notes.explanation: Event-based retention instead starts counting when an event occurs.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Purview Records Management, “Event-based retention”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What kinds of records suit event-based retention? Give two.
notes.back: Any two of: employee records (from end of employment), product records (from discontinuation), contract records (from expiry).
notes.explanation: Each has a lifecycle tied to a business event.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Purview Records Management, “Event-based retention”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is proof of disposition in Records Management?

notes.front: Every item in one project site must be kept for four years, whatever it is. What is the most efficient tool?

B) A sensitivity label
C) A retention label on each document
D) Event-based retention
notes.choicesExplained: B protects content; it does not retain it. C works but means labelling every item. D starts counting from an event, which is not needed here.
notes.explanation: Retention policies give the same settings to everything at site or mailbox level.

notes.front: In a site kept for three years by a retention policy, a few signed agreements must be kept for eight. What do you add?

B) A retention label with an eight-year setting on those agreements
C) A sensitivity label policy
D) Mailbox archiving
notes.choicesExplained: A would apply to the whole site, not only the agreements. C publishes sensitivity labels. D adds mailbox storage.
notes.explanation: Labels set retention at item level, so they can differ from the site’s policy.

notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A document already has a seven-year retention label. A colleague tries to add a second, ten-year retention label alongside it. What happens?
